dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product has pages that are read in an order: the chapters of a guide, the articles of a series, the steps of a course. At the foot of each it offers the page before and the page after, each named by its title, as two large places to press that a reader finds at the same spot on every page.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a pair of previous and next links reads: the gap between its two items and the width under which they stack; an item's corners, padding, edge, the gap between its arrow and its text and between its two lines of text, the two text styles and the arrow's size; the timing of a state change; and the colors of an item's fill, edge, direction label, title, arrow and state layer, at rest and in each state.
rules: A pair of previous and next links offers the page before and the page after the one a person is on, in one sequence. Each item is a link: it has a destination, and without one it is not drawn.
An item is pressed as a whole. Its title is not a second link and is not underlined: the edge, the arrow and its place say what it is.
The direction word (Previous, Next) is the product's, in its language; the arrows are drawn by the component and mirror in a right-to-left layout.
Previous is always at the start and next at the end. Do not swap them, and do not move next to the start when there is no previous page.
State tokens are valued by the design system's pattern rules; override one token or replace the rule.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never style the anchors by hand.

gap.$description: Space between the previous and the next item, side by side or stacked.

shape.$description: The corners of an item, and of its focus ring. The value an outlined card has, because an item is drawn as one.

padding.$description: Space between an item's edge and its content, on every side.

gap.$description: Space between the arrow and the text beside it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product with long page titles stacks its two items sooner than one whose titles are a word or two; another keeps them side by side on a narrow column.

min-width.$description: The least width an item has beside the other one. Where the layout gives the previous and next links less than two of these and the gap, the items stack.

width.$description: The thickness of an item's edge.

typescale.$description: The direction word (Previous, Next) above the title.

gap.$description: Space between the direction word and the title under it.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: An item has no fill at rest; the surface behind it shows through.

color.$description: An item's fill. None at rest: it is where hover, focus and press are drawn.
An item's edge: the one hairline.
The destination's title: the text's own color. An item is pressed as a whole and marked by its edge and its arrow, so its title is not drawn as a text link.
The color hover, focus and press mix into the container: the title's.

feedback-duration.$description: How long the answer to a press takes to spread when sys.behavior.pressed-feedback is ripple: the pressed layer grows from the point of contact over this time, with state-easing. Unused by the other choices.
